expected.title: The leading term of the Euler characteristic of a coherent module twisted by invertible sheaves is given by the lengths at the generic points of the top-dimensional components
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the top-degree behaviour of chi(X, F tensor L_1^{n_1} tensor ... tensor L_r^{n_r}): the difference from the sum of m_i chi(Z_i, L^{n}|_{Z_i}) over the top-dimensional components of the support is a numerical polynomial of total degree strictly less than d = dim Supp(F). The proof recasts the expression as a functional E(F) over integral closed subschemes, proves additivity of E along short exact sequences using additivity of Euler characteristics and of lengths, filters F by subsheaves whose subquotients are pushed-forward ideal sheaves on integral subschemes, reduces to those subquotients, and handles the middle term by the projection formula with the identification of the cohomology of a closed immersion pushforward (proof lines 10311-10385). H3: the reduction through the coherent filtration together with the length-weighted bookkeeping is an independent research-level argument.

expected.title: The composition of two blowing ups in centres of finite presentation is again a blowing up
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if one blows up a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme in a centre of finite presentation and then blows up the result in a further centre of finite presentation, the composite is again a blowing up of the original scheme, in a centre whose underlying closed subset is the union of the first centre with the image of the second (statement lines 8656-8673). The counted proof has two substantive layers: it replaces the second centre, which lives on the blowing up, by a finite type submodule of one power of the first ideal on the base, chosen so that the relevant quotients are supported outside a quasi-compact open, and it then identifies the two candidate blowing ups by comparing ideal sheaves on the second blowing up in the affine local model, where the computation reduces to writing an element as the d-th power of the chosen generator times the corresponding quotient (proof lines 8675-8740). It is H2: the reduction and the local computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard Rees algebra and blowing up statements.

expected.title: The diagonal of the Picard functor of a flat proper family is a locally closed immersion
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes that the diagonal of the Picard functor associated with a flat proper finitely presented family with f_*O_X = O_S is a locally closed immersion, which is the representability step behind the Picard scheme. The non-routine part is the locally-closedness argument rather than the formal diagonal computation. Retained author proof at lines 9217-9304.
